newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products - light ends steady, others fall.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products - light ends steady, others fall.

text.p: Mediterranean oil products were mixed on Wednesday, traders said. Naphtha and gasoline were steady to a touch firmer, while fuel and gas oil slipped lower.
Naphtha held steady with a firm Far East fuelling buying interest but prompt weakness kept offers of fob product scarce.

"A $55-60 fob Med-cif Far East spread has seen around 12 cargoes booked from the Med to the east recently but there are few fob offers now at these weaker levels," a trader said. "I'm looking for fob barrels but just can't find any.
Turkey's Tupras sold up to 35,000 tonnes to Marc Rich through a tender at a premium of $6.2 per tonne over benchmark quotes.
On Tuesday a Greek cargo was reported traded at around benchmark high cif quotes +$8 a tonne to a trader. The cargo was expected to go to the Far East.
Thin local demand was pegged around cif high quotes +$2.
Gasoline advanced early with the effects of tight supplies boosted by higher-than-expected draws in U.S. gasoline stocks, but prices drifted from the early highs in thin trade.
Eurograde cargoes valued $1 firmer at $217.50 cif med.
High sulphur fuel oil looked weak. A trader was heard to have won Turkey's tender for an Aliaga cargo, loading mid month, but the price was not known.
Another trader holding a prompt Turkish piece offered on a floating price basis, a dollar or two below the level paid in the original tender.
Low sulphur fuel oil was steady although falling prices in the U.S. Gulf, at around $13.25 a barrel, put pressure on.
Dealers assessed U.S. numbers, if freight were taken into account, would work out at around $100 cif Italy. But freight was tight and Italian buyers saw no offers far below $105.
Traders and oil consultants assessed Russian fuel oil exports out of the Black Sea and the Baltics in February at 400,000 tonnes and 600,000 tonnes respectively.
